summary: Joseph Haroutunian was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the American University of Beirut, Columbia University (PhD), and Union Theological Seminary. He taught at Wellesley College (1932–1940), McCormick Theological Seminary (1940–1962), and the University of Chicago (1962–1968).

Joseph Loizzo works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst College, Harvard University, and under Robert A. F. Thurman. He served as a visiting scholar at Columbia University and founded the Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science (attested 2007).

Joseph M. Kitagawa worked in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rikkyo University, Church Divinity School of the Pacific, Seabury-Western Theological Seminary, and under Joachim Wach at the University of Chicago (PhD). He served as professor and dean at Chicago.
Joseph Margolis was a philosopher who earned an M.A. from Columbia University (~1947–1950). He held the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University from 1991.

Joseph Marino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 2017), where he studied under Collett Cox and doctoral supervisor Richard Salomon.

Joseph Needham was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Oundle School and Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge. He held long-term posts at the University of Cambridge, Gonville and Caius College, and directed the Needham Research Institute (1976–1990).

Joseph Prabhu is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied under Bernard Williams. He served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007), and held visiting professorships at UCSB, United Theological College, and Bossey.

Joseph Ratzinger worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Munich (~1947–1951) and Ducal Georgianum. He held academic posts at the universities of Munich, Bonn, Münster, Tübingen, and Regensburg between 1958 and 1977.

Joseph Rock worked in sinology and Tibetology. He held positions at the Mid-Pacific Institute (~1908), the University of Hawaiʻi as botanist and curator (1908; 1911–1920), the United States Department of Agriculture (~1920–1924), and the Army Map Service (1944).

Joseph Tiefenthaler was an 18th-century scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a Jesuit missionary in the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773 and was Rector of St. Peter's College, Agra.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A student of Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, he held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, the École des langues orientales, and served as president of the Société Asiatique.

Joseph Vendryes was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1950), École Normale Supérieure (~1904–1907), and the University of Paris (~1907–1946).
Joseph Walser is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenburg, and David S. Pacini.

Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (~1789–1799) and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1847–1849).
Josho Nozawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi. He served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1950).
Joshua Cutler specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ngawang Wangyal and held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (attested 2004).
Joshua Marshman was a scholar of Indology and sinology. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (~1794–1799) and under Johannes Lassar (~1805–1812), and he founded Serampore College in 1818.

Joshua T. Katz is a linguist who studied at Yale, Oxford, and Harvard (PhD 1998). He served as Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998–2022) and became a Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute in 2022.

Josiah Dwight Whitney studied at Yale University (~1836–1839) after attending Round Hill School and Phillips Academy. He held academic posts at the University of Iowa (~1855–1858) and as professor at Harvard University (1865–1896).

Josiah Royce was a philosopher who studied at the University of California, Berkeley, the University of Göttingen under Hermann Lotze, and Johns Hopkins (PhD 1878). He taught at UC Berkeley (~1878–1882) and on the Harvard University faculty from 1882 to 1916.
